title: How do I make a night in feel special?
old_caption: A night in feels special through small choices: one candle, one dish cooked together, phones in a basket by the door and a few good questions to talk through slowly.

title: We text all day but say nothing.
old_caption: Texting all day can still leave you feeling far apart. Swap one message for a real call and ask what's been on their mind. Small talk is only the door; walk through it together.

title: I'm spending the holidays alone.
old_caption: Spending the holidays on your own can still feel warm with a little planning. Cook your favorite, call someone you love, and if an invitation comes, it's okay to say yes.

title: I forgot their birthday.
old_caption: Forgot their birthday? Own it quickly and sincerely, skip the long excuse and make a real plan to make it up. Then put the date in your calendar today, on repeat.

title: My partner is messy. It drives me nuts.
old_caption: Living with a messier partner can test anyone's patience. Pick the one thing that matters most, ask kindly to tackle it together, and let the rest be theirs. It's their home too.

title: My friend is dating someone I don't like.
old_caption: Not loving who your friend is dating is tricky. If it's a real worry, say it once and kindly, tell them you're there either way, and then trust them to choose for themselves.

title: Do I have to tell them about my past?
old_caption: You don't owe anyone your whole story early on. Share your past when the trust is there and at your own pace, and when they open up in return, hold what they tell you gently.

title: They want to settle down. I want to travel.
old_caption: Wanting adventure while your partner wants roots doesn't mean you're mismatched. Say both wishes out loud, then plan a trip together with a home base to come back to.

title: Should I wait for them to change?
old_caption: Hoping someone will change? Give it time, but not forever. Watch what they do more than what they promise, and remember that your time matters too.

title: Can we skip the usual holiday stuff?
old_caption: Skipping the usual holiday plans is allowed. Make a tradition that feels like yours, like pancakes at midnight or a walk in the snow, and let family know early and kindly.
